la:verb:anquiro.gloss: to seek, research, investigate, examine judicially
senses: to seek, research, investigate, examine judicially
la:verb:anquiro.html:
an-quīro, quīsīvi, sītum, 3, v. a.
2. anand quaero
,
to seek on all sides, to look about for, to search after.
Lit. and in gen.: anquirere est circum quaerere, Paul. ex Müll.: anquirere aliquem, apud quem evomet virus, etc.,; so ; .—
Trop., to inquire about, to examine into: aut anquirunt aut consultant, conducat id necne,: anquirentibus nobis omnique acie ingenii contemplantibus,; so ; —
Esp. in judic. lang. t. t.
To institute a careful inquiry or examination: de perduellione,: de morte alicujus,.—
To enter a complaint, to accuse one, with the word designating the punishment in the abl. or gen.: capite anquisitus,: pecuniā anquirere,: cum capitis anquisissent,; .—Hence, anquīsītē, adv., carefully (only in Gell.): satis anquisite satisque sollicite,, where Hertz now reads inquisite.—Comp.: Theophrastus anquisitius super hac ipsā re et exactius pressiusque quam Cicero disserit,, where Hertz now reads inquisitius.
